extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, potential petitioners, and USPTO staff involved in AIA post-issuance proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules implementing AIA inter partes review, post-grant review, and transitional covered business method (CBM) review proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, specifying petition content, institution standards, procedure, timing, discovery, amendment, joinder, and related requirements. Intended to guide petitioners, patent owners, and Board practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules implementing inter partes review, post-grant review, and the transitional program for covered business method patents take effect September 16, 2012 and apply as specified to patents issued before, on, or after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes review rules apply to patents issued before, on, or after Sept 16, 2012 (subpart B). Post-grant review rules generally apply to patents issuing from applications subject to first-inventor-to-file provisions (subpart C). CBM transitional rules apply to any covered business method patent issued before, on, or after Sept 16, 2012 (subpart D).

rubrics_metrics.name: General petition content and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must meet the content and form requirements set by statute and regulation: pay the fee, identify real parties-in-interest, identify with particularity each claim challenged, state grounds for each challenge, and provide supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: include copies of relied-upon patents and printed publications; affidavits/declarations if relying on expert or factual opinions; any other information Director requires; and provide copies of required documents to the patent owner or designated representative. Petitions are made public as soon as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds allowed for inter partes review
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review grounds are limited to issues raised under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 based only on prior art consisting of patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes review cannot be used to challenge under 35 U.S.C. 101 or 112 (except as limited by statute) — those grounds belong to post-grant review when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds allowed for post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant review may challenge any ground that could be raised under 35 U.S.C. 282(b)(2) or (3), including 102, 103 (patents/printed publications), and other grounds such as 101 and 112 (except best mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-grant review is broader than inter partes review; the petition must identify statutory grounds relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limits for filing petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory timing for filing petitions varies by proceeding: post-grant review must be filed not later than nine months after grant or reissue; inter partes petitions may be filed after the later of nine months after grant/reissue or termination of a post-grant review; CBM petitions may be filed any time except during the period in which a post-grant review would be timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation elaborates reissue-claim nuances: petitions cannot request review for reissue-claims identical/narrower than original patent unless within nine months of original patent grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for instituting inter partes review
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review will be instituted only if the Director determines the information in the petition and any preliminary response shows a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least one challenged claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory 'reasonable likelihood' standard (35 U.S.C. 314(a)); the Director must make institution decision within three months after receiving a preliminary response or after the response deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for instituting post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant review will be instituted only if the Director determines the petition would, if unrebutted, demonstrate that it is more likely than not that at least one challenged claim is unpatentable, or that the petition raises a novel or unsettled legal question important to other patents/applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the 'more likely than not' institutional standard (35 U.S.C. 324(a)-(b)); Director's decision likewise must be timely (three-month rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's institution decision is final (nonappealable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's determination whether to institute an inter partes review is final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See statutory provision 35 U.S.C. 314(d) and corresponding rules; notice of institution will be provided in writing and made public, including the date review commences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary response rights and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner has the right to file a preliminary response within a time set by the Director (default three months after filing date for PGR), limited to reasons why no review should be instituted and subject to page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary responses may include evidence except as restricted; preliminary responses may not present new testimonial evidence beyond that already of record except with Board authorization; preliminary responses may not include amendments; patent owner may elect to waive the preliminary response to expedite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing-date requirements for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition is accorded a filing date only when it complies with required content (e.g., §42.204/§42.304), has effected service on the correspondence address of record, and is accompanied by the filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete petitions receive no filing date and will be dismissed if not corrected within one month of notice or before the statutory deadline; a motion to correct clerical/typographical mistakes does not change the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must serve the petition and exhibits on the patent owner at the correspondence address of record; may also serve other known addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon agreement, service may be electronic; personal service is not required; service may be by EXPRESS MAIL® or other means at least as fast and reliable as EXPRESS MAIL®.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year time bar (35 U.S.C. 315(b)) for inter partes review
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review may not be instituted if the petition is filed more than one year after the date on which the petitioner, real party-in-interest, or privy was served with a complaint alleging infringement of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time limitation does not apply to requests for joinder under 35 U.S.C. 315(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel effects (35 U.S.C. 315(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inter partes review results in a final written decision, the petitioner (and real parties in interest/privies) may be estopped from requesting or maintaining a proceeding before the Office or certain civil/ITC proceedings on any ground that was raised or reasonably could have been raised during that review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estoppel prevents relitigation of grounds within specified fora; settlement-termination rules affect whether estoppel attaches (see 35 U.S.C. 317).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder rules and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may join as a party to an instituted review any person who properly files a petition and whose petition warrants institution; requests for joinder must be filed as a motion no later than one month after the institution date of the review for which joinder is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joinder may be requested by patent owner or petitioner; certain timing rules (e.g., §42.101(b) exceptions) apply when joinder is sought along with a petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — single initial motion and additional motions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may file one motion to amend (cancel or propose substitute claims) only after conferring with the Board and normally no later than the patent owner response; additional motions require Board authorization and may be permitted for good cause or to materially advance settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reasonable number of substitute claims is presumed to be one substitute per challenged claim (rebuttable). Motions may be denied if they do not respond to a ground involved in the trial, enlarge scope, or introduce new matter. Board will consider supplemental information submitted by petitioner after the motion-to-amend filing period when deciding authorization for additional motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend must include a claim listing, clearly show changes, and set forth support in the original disclosure for each added/amended claim and any earlier-filed disclosure relied upon for benefit of an earlier filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must not introduce new matter or enlarge claim scope; support must be shown by citations to specification or earlier disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information submission timing and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: After institution, a party may file a motion to submit supplemental information if requested within one month of institution and relevant to a claim under trial. Late or non-relevant supplemental information requires authorization showing why it could not have been earlier obtained and that consideration would be in the interests of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners seeking to submit late information must meet a two-prong showing: (1) reasonable inability to obtain earlier, and (2) interests-of-justice justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery is limited: generally limited to deposition of witnesses who submitted affidavits/declarations and to what is otherwise necessary in the interest of justice; additional discovery requires a showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery is confined to evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced by either party. The Director's regulations prescribe sanctions for abuse of discovery or process and provide for protective orders for confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: In an inter partes review, the petitioner bears the burden of proving unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allocation is statutory (35 U.S.C. 316(e)) and applies to inter partes proceedings instituted under chapter 31.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to final written decision and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will issue a final written decision not later than one year after the date the Director notices institution, subject to extension by up to six months for good cause and adjustment in cases of joinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations permit adjustments of time periods in the case of joinder; for CBM, pendency after institution normally no more than one year, extendable by up to six months by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response after institution
rubrics_metrics.description: After institution, a patent owner may file a response addressing any grounds not denied; the response is filed as an opposition and is subject to page limits and timing rules (default three months from institution if not ordered otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner response may include affidavits/declarations and is the vehicle for contesting grounds instituted into trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to correct clerical/typographical mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may file a motion seeking to correct clerical or typographical mistakes in a petition; the grant of such a motion does not change the petition's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to fix non-substantive errors without affecting timeliness determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory disclaimer by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a statutory disclaimer under 35 U.S.C. 253(a), and no post-grant review will be instituted based on disclaimed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimers remove claims from contention for institution purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility and sealing of filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The file of any proceeding will be made available to the public except that documents filed with intent to be sealed will be treated as sealed pending a ruling on a motion to seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations provide for protective orders and procedures for handling business-confidential information; certain agreements filed in connection with settlements may be treated as business confidential information on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party has the right to an oral hearing as part of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing procedures and timing are governed by the Board's rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and other format constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary responses and patent owner responses are subject to page limits under § 42.24 and other format/filing constraints specified in subpart A and related provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must comply with these limits or seek relief from the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered Business Method (CBM) petition eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may not file a CBM review petition unless the petitioner, its real party-in-interest, or a privy has been sued for or charged with infringement of the patent; 'charged with infringement' means a real and substantial controversy such that the petitioner would have standing to bring a declaratory judgment action in Federal court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must also demonstrate that the patent is a covered business method patent and meet other eligibility requirements in § 42.302 and content rules in § 42.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBM petition content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM petitions must request judgment against specific patent claims and (in addition to general petition requirements) identify the claim, statutory grounds (35 U.S.C. 282(b)(2) or (3) as modified by AIA §18(a)(1)(C)), claim construction (including 112(f) means/step-plus-function mappings), how the construed claim is unpatentable, and exhibit numbers with specific relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may exclude or give no weight to evidence where relevance or supporting portions are not identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard in CBM and unexpired patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim in an unexpired patent, including for CBM review, is given its broadest reasonable construction in light of the specification in which it appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction standard is applied for CBM proceedings under these rules (see § 42.300(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on number of post-grant reviews in first four years
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose a limit on the number of post-grant reviews instituted during each of the first four one-year periods in which 35 U.S.C. 321 is in effect if the number equals or exceeds the number of inter partes reexaminations ordered in the last fiscal year prior to the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such limits would be announced via the Official Gazette or Federal Register; petitions filed after a limit is reached will be deemed untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific petition content requirements — mapping claims to prior art / statutory deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: For prior-art-based grounds, the petition must specify where each element of the claim is found in the prior art; for other grounds, the petition must identify specific parts of the claim that fail to comply and state how they fail; the petition must supply exhibit numbers and identify specific portions that support the challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may exclude or give no weight to evidence when relevance or specific supporting portions are not stated.
